sourceReview.finding: server.stop() runs at the beginning of afterEach, before error-ledger attachment/assertion. This does not explain these errors because both precede afterEach by more than four seconds.
Page-side hasOfflineApp encloses its cache keys/open/match awaits in try/catch and returns false on rejection.
The service-worker registration promise chain has a catch handler. The observed payload does not prove an unhandled registration rejection.
The public document cache-shell lookup already catches unavailable cache storage and continues to network.

Independent concrete availability gap: the eligible public-asset response awaits publicCacheMatch without a cache-rejection fallback. If keys/open/match rejects, fetch(request) is never attempted even when the network is available. This is a source-established failure path, not proof that it emitted these recorded pageerrors.

proposedNarrowFixNotApplied.scope: public/sw.js eligible asset branch and existing actual-template VM tests only, after an explicit parent source11 fix window.
proposedNarrowFixNotApplied.behavior: Try the same public cache lookup and return a cache hit; catch only that lookup failure; then return fetch(request) outside the catch. Preserve original request, network failures, eligibility checks and install-only cache writes.
regressionPlan: Root and subpath bases times keys/open/match rejection: online asset returns network exactly once with the original request.
Cache contents and installation write count unchanged by runtime fallback.
Available cache hit still avoids network.
Network failure remains a rejected request, with no invented successful response.
Existing query/private/auth/API/cross-origin/out-of-scope bypass and immutable previous-build-cache tests remain required.
proposedNarrowFixNotApplied.executionStatus: NOT RUN; source10 frozen runs are still active.

limits: No evidence links the errors specifically to font loading or IndexedDB.
No trace event identifies an unhandledrejection handler or its originating promise; pageerror alone does not isolate that ownership.
Some navigation HAR receive durations exceed the case lifetime; those are excluded from transport timing conclusions.
A later serial confirmation cannot erase these original failed runs.
